review_notes: Reviewed all lines 1–199, the underlying coefficient, envelope, reference-family and sum definitions, and related recentering and narrow-tail uses. The proposed generalization is source-supported but was not tested in Lean.

findings.excerpt:
theorem referenceSelf_constant :
    (Q).constant = P.absoluteConstant*(F*cone+2) := by
  unfold constant absoluteConstant referenceFamily
  ring

theorem referenceSelf_absoluteConstant : (Q).absoluteConstant = P.absoluteConstant := rfl
findings.problem: These constant identities are restricted to equal old and new reference slopes through Q. Neither constant depends on those slopes, while the surrounding API also uses genuinely recentered families.
findings.proposed_change: Generalize both declarations by introducing `(oldSlope newSlope : ℝ)`. With the existing parameters and hypotheses, the exact conclusions are `(P.referenceFamily oldSlope newSlope R cone w F hw hcone hF hwide hfrequency).constant = P.absoluteConstant * (F * cone + 2)` and `(P.referenceFamily oldSlope newSlope R cone w F hw hcone hF hwide hfrequency).absoluteConstant = P.absoluteConstant`. The existing unfolding-and-ring proof and rfl proof respectively apply: referenceFamily preserves order, profileBound and ratioBound and sets carrierBound to F*cone. Retain the self-specialized forms as corollaries if needed. No nonemptiness or positivity of R is required; empty families, N = 0, cone = 0 and F = 0 remain covered.
findings.benefit: Users estimating recentered reference families can reuse the same carrier-cost identities without unfolding implementation details or reproving the algebra.
